subject.title: Validate required run artifacts against a schema (`--require-artifact-schema`)

question: Should Crabbox core expose artifact-content schema validation, and what schema compatibility contract should the public flag promise?
rationale: This adds a permanent CLI/configuration surface and defines validation semantics that repositories may rely on as proof; source inspection cannot determine whether maintainers want a limited dialect, full JSON Schema compatibility, or repository-owned validation.

options.title: Approve a bounded core gate
options.body: Sponsor the linked PR after it clearly names the supported schema dialect, adds a fetched-byte cap, preserves capability-driven provider boundaries, and supplies real SSH-backed proof.

options.title: Require standard JSON Schema
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require a maintained standards-compatible validator instead of a silent custom subset before exposing the flag.

options.title: Keep validation repository-owned
options.body: Decline the new core surface and continue requiring each run command to validate its own evidence before Crabbox performs the existence gate.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded core gate
recommendation.body: Sponsor the linked PR after it clearly names the supported schema dialect, adds a fetched-byte cap, preserves capability-driven provider boundaries, and supplies real SSH-backed proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent core CLI/provider work and explicit invitation to this discussion make them the best available owner for the public product-contract choice.
